LESSON: SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY OF BUSINESS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: BUSINESS STUDIES
Strand: Business and its Environment
Topic 2.3: Social Responsibility of Business
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Social Responsibility of Business, part of Business and its Environment in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 BUSINESS STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: when carrying out social responsibilities, Why is business social responsibility important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. justify the need for social responsibility of a business in the society,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Social Responsibility of Business in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. examine social responsibility activities of a business in the community,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Social Responsibility of Business in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. analyse the challenges faced by businesses when carrying out social responsibilities,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Social Responsibility of Business in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. design and implement a social responsibility activity in the school,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Social Responsibility of Business in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate the need for business social responsibility in the society and the environment. ● in groups, guide learners to discuss and present on the need for social responsibility of a business in the society, ● learners use digital resources with assistive technology or print media to search on social responsibility activities of a business in the community, ● in pairs, learners are guided to discuss how businesses can support safe road use in the community, ● learners are guided to brainstorm and present on the challenges faced by businesses when carrying out social responsibilities, Why is business social responsibility important? 21 ● in groups, learners are guided to carry out a simple survey to identify needy learners, ● guide learners to mobilize the available resources from the local community to assist the needy learners.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Social Responsibility of Business in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Social Responsibility of Business together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: learner develops effective communication skills when brainstorming and presenting on the challenges

faced by businesses when carrying out social responsibility.

● Critical thinking and problem solving: learner develops interpretation and inference skills when carrying out a survey

to identify the needy learners.

● Creativity and imagination: learner strengthens networking skills when mobilising resources from the local

community.

● Citizenship: learner enhances social cultural sensitivity and awareness skills when mobilizing the resources from

the local community to assist the needy in the society.

Values:
● Unity: learner cooperates with others when sharing digital resources or print media to search on social

responsibility activities of a business in the community.

● Responsibility: learner exercises accountability as they mobilize the available resources from local community to

assist the needy learners.

● Love: learner shows compassion as they mobilize the resources and shares out to the needy learners.

● Social justice: learner exercises equity as they share out mobilized resources equitably.

22

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Peer Education and Mentorship: interpersonal relationships are enhanced as learner discusses how businesses can

support safe road use in the community.

● Social cohesion is promoted as learner mobilise available resources to assist needy learners.
